Dr B White
Neurosurgeon
City Hospital
Newtown Hospital
05/07/2014
Dear Dr White,
Regarding Mr George Poulos,
I am writing to refer Mr Poulus, a 45-year-old stockbroker, whose features are suggestive of discogenic back pain with radiculopathy.
On 21-06-2014, Mr Poulos firstly presented with a 2-day history of back pain after lifting a heavy object. It was a sudden severe pain in the mid lower back which locked him in a semi-flexed position. It was not associated with any radiation to the thigh. The pain improved gradually and he was able to walk around his house. On examination, there was a limited extension of the lumbar spine by pain which exaggerated also during flexion of his fingertips to the patella. Accordingly, I advised him to take sick leave in addition to analgesic medication prescription. One week later, there was a progression of the pain to the back of the thigh, lateral calf and the foot.
On today's review, Mr Poulos' condition deteriorated as he was not able to perform any lumbar flexion. His movement was restricted by pain in addition to loss of sensation of the distal calf and in the planter aspect of foot. Furthermore, right ankle reflex was lost.
In view of the above, I would be grateful if you could assess Mr Poulos and request further investigation including an MRI. Your advice regarding surgical option as a management would be appreciated.
For any queries,please contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
